params.script_inline:
import sys, json, uuid

# Seeds the authoring prompt. The corpus is no longer PREFETCHED into this
# prompt: it is one of four tools the model may call, so what travels from here
# is the duty (head), the grammar of a declaration (GRAMMAR) and the tool menu
# -- and the request stays a user turn, because a model told "here is the
# corpus" writes about the corpus while a model told "here is the request"
# writes about the request.
doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
ctx = (doc["envelope"].get("header") or {}).get("context") or {}
msgs = doc["body"].get("messages") or []

request = ""
for m in msgs:
    if m.get("origin") == "user" and m.get("text"):
        request = m["text"]

# A build is a THREAD now, not a single pass: the round-trip through the tools
# has to be able to name what it belongs to. Minted here, once, because this is
# the only cell every build passes through exactly once.
build_id = str(ctx.get("build_id") or "").strip() or uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]

head = ("You are drafting a MANIFEST for a meclaw colony: an ordered list of "
        "mutation declarations, each {\"scope\": <path>, \"ctx\": {}, "
        "\"diff\": {...}}. The diff keys you may use are add_nodes, "
        "remove_nodes, add_edges, remove_edges, swap_nodes and move_nodes -- "
        "no others exist. Answer with ONE json object "
        "{\"declarations\": [...]} and nothing else. "
        "The manifest rolls FORWARD and stops at the first refusal, with no "
        "rollback, so order the declarations so that a partial application is "
        "never worse than none.")

scope = str(ctx.get("build_scope") or "")
if scope:
    head += (" Every declaration you write must name the scope %r or a path "
             "beneath it; that is what the requester asked for and what the "
             "submitter will let through." % scope)

# The ENTRY SHAPE of a declaration, and the one topology rule that decides
# whether what you wrote is reachable. It rides in the HEAD rather than in the
# retrieved patterns, because a corpus outage is when a model needs it most.
# Measured: three drafts of a capable hosted model, three schema refusals at
# declaration 1, every one of them on the shape of an add_nodes entry
# (plans/welle-2026-08-27/receipts/s12-luna-run.md). After that block landed the
# same model encoded every entry correctly and was refused one level higher:
# `requirement_missing`, because it named templates whose `requires` contract it
# did not meet. So REQUIREMENTS rides here too, and the catalogue row it points
# at leads with the contract line (workshop/tools/build_librarian_seed.py).
GRAMMAR = (
    "GRAMMAR -- this is the part that gets refused. An add_nodes entry is "
    "{\"name\": \"<name under the scope>\", \"template\": \"<a template that "
    "exists>\"}: both keys are REQUIRED and they are the only way to place a "
    "cell. There is no \"path\" key, no \"kind\" key and no \"type\" key, and "
    "there is no way to ask for a bare cell type -- every node is an instance "
    "of a template that exists, so name one. An add_edges entry is "
    "{\"from\": \"./x\", \"to\": \"./y\"} with scope-relative paths, plus an "
    "optional \"condition\" and \"modifier\".\n\n"
    "ENDPOINTS -- an edge endpoint has exactly two legal spellings, and the "
    "door checks them before it looks at anything else. \"./x\" names "
    "something standing directly under the scope; \"./x/y\" names something "
    "deeper under it, at any depth. Everything else is refused. \".\" is NOT "
    "an endpoint -- the scope is not a node, and the refusal reads "
    "edge_schema from='.' unknown. An endpoint that begins with \"/\" or "
    "contains \"..\" is refused as scope_out_of_bounds, even when it points "
    "INSIDE the scope. And both endpoints must name something that already "
    "stands under the scope or that this manifest creates -- in this "
    "declaration or an earlier one; an edge naming anything else is refused "
    "with edge_schema and the manifest stops there.\n\n"
    "CONNECTIVITY -- activity is derived from the edges alone. A cell is "
    "active as soon as ANY edge touches it, but a HIVE is active only while "
    "an edge crosses its boundary: an edge between a hive and its own child "
    "is internal and connects nothing, and an inactive hive drags its whole "
    "subtree down with it. So if the unit you are filling already exists and "
    "is reachable, one edge from something beside your new cell is enough. "
    "But if this manifest CREATES the unit, its crossing edge cannot be drawn "
    "from inside it -- the scope is not an endpoint -- so SCOPE THE "
    "DECLARATION ONE LEVEL UP: at the parent, name the node \"c/<name>\", "
    "and draw both the door into the unit (./c to ./c/<name> and back) and "
    "at least one edge between ./c and something already standing beside it "
    "-- that second pair is what makes it active. Call graph_read on that "
    "parent scope to see what is there to cross from.\n\n"
    "REQUIREMENTS -- a template may DEMAND keys before it can be instantiated, "
    "and the catalogue row of every template opens with a line that says which "
    "(it begins CONTRACT --). Required ctx keys go into the \"ctx\" block of the "
    "very declaration that names the template; there is no other channel for "
    "them, and override_params is not one -- that sets a cell's own params. "
    "`ctx` is mutation-wide, so every node of that declaration gets the same "
    "value: two nodes needing different values need two declarations. Required "
    "ENV keys belong to the colony and you cannot supply them at all -- if a "
    "template demands one, it is only instantiable where the operator already "
    "set it. A declaration that names a template without its required ctx keys "
    "is refused with requirement_missing, and nothing of the manifest is "
    "applied. So read the CONTRACT line of every template you name, and if you "
    "cannot meet it, name a template you can. Example of a declaration that "
    "meets one:\n"
    "{\"scope\": \"/a/b\", \"ctx\": {\"model\": \"<the model id>\"}, "
    "\"diff\": {\"add_nodes\": [{\"name\": \"brain\", \"template\": "
    "\"some-template-whose-contract-asks-for-model\"}]}}\n\n"
    "EXAMPLE of one declaration, into a scope that already stands:\n"
    "{\"scope\": \"/a/b\", \"ctx\": {}, \"diff\": {\"add_nodes\": "
    "[{\"name\": \"fetch\", \"template\": \"web-fetch-tool\"}], \"add_edges\": "
    "[{\"from\": \"./dispatch\", \"to\": \"./fetch\"}, "
    "{\"from\": \"./fetch\", \"to\": \"./collector\"}]}}\n\n"
    "EXAMPLE of the same cell placed inside a unit this manifest fills, "
    "declared at the unit's PARENT because the scope is not an endpoint:\n"
    "{\"scope\": \"/a/b\", \"ctx\": {}, \"diff\": {\"add_nodes\": "
    "[{\"name\": \"c/fetch\", \"template\": \"web-fetch-tool\"}], "
    "\"add_edges\": [{\"from\": \"./c\", \"to\": \"./c/fetch\"}, "
    "{\"from\": \"./c/fetch\", \"to\": \"./c\"}, "
    "{\"from\": \"./dispatch\", \"to\": \"./c\"}, "
    "{\"from\": \"./c\", \"to\": \"./dispatch\"}]}}")

# The tools, and the whole of them. A closed vocabulary is what makes this
# builder concretely buildable where a general harness cannot be: every tool
# answers a refusal this system has actually produced.
#
#   requirement_missing  -> catalogue_lookup (the row that opens `CONTRACT --`)
#   the ISLAND           -> graph_read (activity is edge-derived, so it SHOWS)
#   the wrong template   -> registry_read + catalogue_lookup
#
# There is no hand here and there will not be one: submitting is the requester's,
# under the identity the substrate stamped on the envelope (ADR-0015).
TOOLS = {
    "librarian_search": {
        "description": "Search the builder's corpus (spec sections, cookbook "
                       "patterns, rewiring shapes) with BM25. Use it before "
                       "writing a shape you are not sure of.",
        "parameters": {"type": "object",
                       "properties": {"query": {"type": "string"}},
                       "required": ["query"]}},
    "catalogue_lookup": {
        "description": "Look up templates by name or purpose. Every row opens "
                       "with a CONTRACT line naming the ctx and env keys an "
                       "instantiation owes. Call this for EVERY template you "
                       "intend to name.",
        "parameters": {"type": "object",
                       "properties": {"query": {"type": "string"}},
                       "required": ["query"]}},
    "graph_read": {
        "description": "Read the live topology under a scope: which cells exist "
                       "and which edges connect them. Use it to check that what "
                       "you are about to draw crosses into the unit it must "
                       "reach.",
        "parameters": {"type": "object",
                       "properties": {"scope": {"type": "string"}},
                       "required": ["scope"]}},
    "registry_read": {
        "description": "Read which cells stand under a path and whether they "
                       "are active. Use it to see what is already there before "
                       "adding beside it.",
        "parameters": {"type": "object",
                       "properties": {"path_prefix": {"type": "string"},
                                      "cell_type": {"type": "string"},
                                      "active": {"type": "boolean"},
                                      "limit": {"type": "number"}},
                       "required": ["path_prefix"]}},
}

# The retrieval guarantee rides HERE, in the instructions, and not in a tool
# result: agentically a result is an observation the model may overrule, and a
# duty that can be overruled is not one. Same argument that put GRAMMAR here.
TOOLING = (
    "TOOLS -- you have four eyes and no hand. Nothing you call applies "
    "anything; submitting is done by whoever asked, under their own identity. "
    "Look BEFORE you write: call catalogue_lookup for every template you intend "
    "to name, because its CONTRACT line is the only place the ctx keys it "
    "demands are published, and call graph_read on the scope you are drawing "
    "into, because a unit no edge crosses into is born inactive and nothing "
    "will reach it. Answering without a single call is allowed and is almost "
    "always wrong. When you have what you need, answer with the manifest and "
    "no tool calls.")

sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
    "header": {"route": "compose", "operation": "brief", "build_id": build_id},
    "system": {
        "instructions": {"text": head + "\n\n" + GRAMMAR + "\n\n" + TOOLING},
        "tools": {name: {"text": json.dumps(
            {"type": "function", "function": {"name": name, **schema}})}
            for name, schema in TOOLS.items()}},
    "messages": [{"origin": "user", "type": "text", "id": "", "text": request}]}))

description.purpose: Seeds the authoring prompt: the duty, the grammar of a mutation declaration and the tool menu (system.tools.*), with the request left as a user turn. The corpus is not prefetched here -- it is one of four eyes the model may call, so what this cell guarantees is the part a tool result must never be able to overrule.
description.use_when: At the head of a build, on hop.route == 'brief'.
description.not_in_scope: No retrieval of its own and no tool calling of its own: it publishes the four schemas and mints the build_id, and every call is the composer's. No hand either -- submitting belongs to whoever asked, under their own identity (ADR-0015).
